edit.description: `SHAPE_PATTERNS` (line 1130) is a hand-listed `[(Shape, regex::Regex); 3]` beside the exhaustive `Shape::pattern` (1179) / `match_holds` (1192) matches — a private partial copy of the closed `Shape` set. Replace the array-plus-`find` lookup in `Shape::admits` (1202) with a per-variant `match` over one `LazyLock<regex::Regex>` static each, every static compiling `Shape::pattern()` so the name-to-expression mapping keeps its one home. While the file is open, the `SHAPE_PATTERNS` doc comment's stale cite `tests/shape_predicate.rs` corrects to `tests/it/shape_predicate.rs`.

summary: The compiled shape-regex table hand-lists the `Shape` enum, so a fourth variant falls through `admits` instead of failing to compile.

per.section: A shared concept is one type

tests.asserts: unchanged and green — each of the three shipped shapes still decides its documented rule in both directions, and an unknown shape name is still refused at load

acceptance: `cargo test` and `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` green, with the shape-to-regex lookup an exhaustive `match`: adding a `Shape` variant stops compiling rather than resolving to no pattern.
notes: Verified on disk: `admits` looks its shape up with `.find().is_some_and(...)`, so an absent entry yields `matched = false`; a negative-polarity shape (`match_holds` false, like `no-xml-tags`) then reads as holding for every value — a silent green, the failure class 'A green verdict is proven non-vacuous' names. The regression pin is the type rather than a test: a per-variant match cannot be written incomplete, and no Rust test can add a variant. scoped at 2ae79534
